readings.title: Captive Integration and Covenant Dignity
readings.subtitle: Regulating the humane integration of foreign women into Israelite households.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 21:10] “When you go out to fight against your enemies, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> them into your hand, and you shall take <dn>את</dn> them captive, [11] and shall see among the captives a woman fair of form, and shall delight in her and take her for your wife, [12] then you shall bring her home to your house, and she shall shave her head and trim her nails, [13] and put aside <dn>את</dn> the mantle of her captivity, and shall dwell in your house, and mourn <dn>את</dn> her father and <dn>את</dn> her mother a month of days. And after that you shall go in to her and be her husband, and she shall be your wife. [14] “And it shall be, if you are not pleased with her, then you shall let her go at her desire, but you do not sell her at all for silver. Do not treat her harshly, since you have humbled her.

readings.title: The Inviolable Right of the Firstborn
readings.subtitle: Inheritance is governed by chronological truth, not emotional preference.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 21:15] “When a man has two wives, one loved and the other unloved, and they have borne him children, both the loved and the unloved, and the first-born son is of her who is unloved, [16] then it shall be, on the day he makes his sons to inherit his possessions, he is not allowed to treat <dn>את</dn> the son of the beloved wife as first-born in the face of the son of the unloved, who is truly the first-born. [17] “But he is to acknowledge <dn>את</dn> the son of the unloved wife as the first-born by giving him a double portion of all that he has, for he is the beginning of his strength – the right of the first-born is his.

readings.title: Purging Systemic Rebellion
readings.subtitle: Removing incurable disharmony from the family and the national framework.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 21:18] “When a man has a wayward and rebellious son who is not listening to the voice of his father or the voice of his mother, and who, when they have disciplined him, does not listen to them, [19] then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city, to the gate of his city, [20] and shall say to the elders of his city, ‘This son of ours is wayward and rebellious. He is not listening to our voice, he is a glutton and a drunkard.’ [21] “Then all the men of his city shall stone him to death with stones. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst. And let all Yisra’ěl hear, and fear.

readings.title: The Limit of Execution and Land Sanctity
readings.subtitle: Preventing the defilement of the physical inheritance by promptly burying the accursed.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 21:22] “And when a man has committed a sin worthy of death, then he shall be put to death and you shall hang <dn>את</dn> him on a tree. [23] “Let his body not remain overnight on the tree, for you shall certainly bury him the same day – for he who is hanged is accursed of <dn>Elohim</dn> – so that you do not defile <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you as an inheritance.

readings.title: The Economics of Premial Brotherhood
readings.subtitle: Active responsibility in preserving and restoring a neighbor's property and livelihood.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 22:1] “When you see <dn>את</dn> your brother’s ox or <dn>את</dn> his sheep straying away, you shall not hide yourself from them. Return them to your brother without fail. [2] “And if your brother is not near you, or if you do not know him, then you shall bring it to your own house, and it shall be with you until your brother seeks it, then you shall return it to him. [3] “And so you do with his donkey, and so you do with his garment, and so you do with whatever your brother loses, which he has lost and you have found. You are not allowed to hide yourself. [4] “When you see <dn>את</dn> your brother’s donkey or <dn>את</dn> his ox fall down on the way, you shall not hide yourself from them. Help him raise them without fail.

readings.title: The Absolute Boundary of Gender Design
readings.subtitle: Rejecting the abomination of blurring YeHoVaH's created distinctions.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 22:5] “A woman does not wear that which pertains to a man, nor does a man put on a woman’s garment, for whoever does this is an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: Sustainable Harvesting and Biological Respect
readings.subtitle: Preserving the mother to ensure the continuity of the ecological cycle.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 22:6] “When you come upon a bird’s nest along the way, in any tree or on the ground, with young ones or eggs, with the mother sitting on the young or on the eggs, do not take the mother with the young – [7] let the mother go without fail, and take <dn>את</dn> the young for yourself, so that it might be well with you, and that you shall prolong your days.

readings.title: Preemptive Civil Liability
readings.subtitle: Establishing physical safeguards to prevent blood-guilt within the community framework.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 22:8] “When you build a new house, then you shall make a parapet for your roof, so that you do not bring blood-guilt on your house when one falls from it.

readings.title: The Prohibition of Unnatural Mixtures
readings.subtitle: Maintaining systemic purity and designated purpose in agriculture and textiles.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 22:9] “Do not sow your vineyard with different kinds of seed, lest the yield of the seed which you have sown and the fruit of your vineyard be defiled. [10] “Do not plough with an ox and a donkey together. [11] “Do not put on a garment of different kinds, of wool and linen together.

readings.title: The Visual Mark of Covenant Loyalty
readings.subtitle: Wearing tassels as a constant, physical reminder of the overarching legal framework.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 22:12] “Make tassels on the four corners of the garment with which you cover yourself.

readings.title: Defending the Covenant of Marital Purity
readings.subtitle: Legal procedures for validating maidenhood and penalizing fraudulent accusations.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 22:13] “When any man takes a wife, and shall go in to her, and shall hate her, [14] and shall make abusive charges against her and bring an evil name on her and say, ‘<dn>I</dn> took <dn>את</dn> this woman, and when <dn>I</dn> came to her <dn>I</dn> did not find her a maiden,’ [15] then the father and mother of the young woman shall take and bring out <dn>את</dn> the proof of the girl’s maidenhood to the elders of the city at the gate. [16] “And the girl’s father shall say to the elders, ‘<dn>I</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> my daughter to this man as wife, and he hates her. [17] And see, he has made abusive charges against her, saying, “<dn>I</dn> did not find <dn>את</dn> your daughter a maiden,” and yet these are the proofs of my daughter’s maidenhood.’ And they shall spread <dn>את</dn> the garment before the elders of the city. [18] “And the elders of that city shall take <dn>את</dn> that man and punish him, [19] and fine him one hundred pieces of silver and give them to the father of the young woman, because he has brought an evil name on a maiden of Yisra’ěl. And she is to be his wife, he is not allowed to put her away all his days. [20] “But if the matter is true, that the girl was not found a maiden, [21] then they shall bring out <dn>את</dn> the girl to the door of her father’s house, and the men of her city shall stone her to death with stones, because she has done wickedness in Yisra’ěl, to whore in her father’s house. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst.

readings.title: The Penalty for Covenant Infidelity
readings.subtitle: Purging the extreme disharmony of adultery from the national assembly.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 22:22] “When a man is found lying with a woman married to a husband, then both of them shall die, both the man that lay with the woman, and the woman. Thus you shall purge the evil from Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: Judgments on Assault and Consent
readings.subtitle: Distinguishing between mutual rebellion and physical overpowerment.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 22:23] “When a girl who is a maiden is engaged to a husband, and a man finds her in the city and lies with her, [24] then you shall bring them both out to the gate of that city, and shall stone them to death with stones, the girl because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he has humbled <dn>את</dn> his neighbour’s wife. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst. [25] “But if a man finds <dn>את</dn> the girl who is engaged in the field, and the man takes hold of her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die. [26] “But you shall do no matter to the girl. The girl has no sin worthy of death – for the matter is like a man who rises against his neighbour and murders him – a being – [27] for he found her in the field, and she cried out, the engaged girl, but without anyone to save her.

readings.title: Restitution for Unengaged Violation
readings.subtitle: Enforcing lifelong responsibility and economic penalty for unauthorized taking.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 22:28] “When a man finds a girl who is a maiden, who is not engaged, and he seizes her and lies with her, and they are found out, [29] then the man who lay with her shall give to the girl’s father fifty pieces of silver, and she is to be his wife because he has humbled her. He is not allowed to put her away all his days.

readings.title: The Prohibition of Paternal Usurpation
readings.subtitle: Maintaining the absolute boundary of a father's intimate domain.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 22:30] “A man does not take <dn>את</dn> his father’s wife, nor uncover his father’s skirt.

readings.title: Biological and Generational Exclusions
readings.subtitle: Restricting entry into the community due to foundational physical or covenantal corruption.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 23:1] “He who is wounded by crushing of testicles or whose penis is cut off, shall not enter into the community of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [2] “A mamzer shall not enter the community of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, even a tenth generation of his shall not enter the community of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Permanent Exile of Ammon and Mo'ab
readings.subtitle: The eternal consequence for economically and spiritually attacking the camp.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 23:3] “An Ammonite or Mo’aḇite shall not enter the assembly of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, even a tenth generation of them shall not ever enter the assembly of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [4] because they did not meet you with bread and water on the way when you came out of Mitsrayim, and because they hired against you <dn>את</dn> Bil‛am son of Be‛or from Pethor of Aram Naharayim, to curse you. [5] “But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> refused to listen to Bil‛am, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> turned the curse into a blessing for you, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> loves you. [6] “Do not seek their peace nor their good, all your days, forever.

readings.title: Conditional Integration of Edom and Mitsrayim
readings.subtitle: Acknowledging brotherly ties and historical refuge after the third generation.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 23:7] “Do not loathe an Eḏomite, for he is your brother. Do not loathe a Mitsrian, because you were a stranger in his land. [8] “The children of the third generation born to them do enter the assembly of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Physical Sanctity of the Military Camp
readings.subtitle: Maintaining strict hygiene and purity, for the Creator walks in the camp's midst.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 23:9] “When the camp goes out against your enemies, then you shall guard yourself from every evil matter. [10] “When there is any man among you who is not clean because of an emission in the night, then he shall go outside the camp. Let him not come into the midst of the camp. [11] “And it shall be, at the approach of evening, that he bathes with water. And when the sun sets let him come into the midst of the camp. [12] “And you shall have a place outside the camp, where you shall go out, [13] and you shall have a sharp implement among your equipment, and when you sit down outside, you shall dig with it and turn and cover <dn>את</dn> your excrement. [14] “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you and give <dn>את</dn> your enemies over to you. Therefore your camp shall be set-apart, so that <dn>He</dn> does not see unclean matter among you, and shall turn away from you.

readings.title: Asylum for the Escaped Slave
readings.subtitle: Providing safe harbor from oppressive foreign masters without exploitation.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 23:15] “You do not hand over to his master the slave who has escaped from his master to you. [16] “Let him dwell with you in your midst, in the place which he chooses within one of your gates, where it is pleasing to him. Do not oppress him.

readings.title: The Ban on Cultic Prostitution
readings.subtitle: Forbidding the financial proceeds of systemic physical and spiritual adultery.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 23:17] “None of the daughters of Yisra’ěl is to be a cult prostitute, nor any of the sons of Yisra’ěl be a cult prostitute. [18] “Do not bring <dn>את</dn> the harlot-fee of a whore or the pay of a dog to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> for any vowed offering, for both of these are an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: The Economics of Interest-Free Brotherhood
readings.subtitle: Facilitating premial wealth within Israel while charging standard usury to foreigners.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 23:19] “Do not lend at interest to your brother, interest of silver, interest of food, or interest of whatever is lent at interest. [20] “To a foreigner you lend at interest, but to your brother you do not lend at interest, so that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> might bless you in all that you put your hand to in the land which you are entering to possess.

readings.title: The Integrity of the Spoken Vow
readings.subtitle: Strict accountability for voluntary verbal commitments made before the Creator.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 23:21] “When you make a vow to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, do not delay to pay it, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is certainly requiring it of you, and it shall be sin in you. [22] “But when you abstain from vowing, it is not sin in you. [23] “That which has gone from your lips you shall guard and do, for you voluntarily vowed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> what you have promised with your mouth.

readings.title: The Boundary Between Gleaning and Theft
readings.subtitle: Allowing immediate satisfaction of hunger without exploiting a neighbor's capital.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 23:24] “When you come into your neighbour’s vineyard, you shall eat to the satisfaction of your desire, but do not put any in a receptacle of yours. [25] “When you come into your neighbour’s standing grain, you shall pluck the heads with your hand, but do not use a sickle on your neighbour’s standing grain.

readings.title: The Limitation of Retributive Corporal Punishment
readings.subtitle: Restricting physical blows to prevent the systemic degradation of a brother.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 25:1] “When there is a dispute between men, then they shall come unto judgment, and they shall be judged, and the righteous declared righteous and the wrongdoer declared wrong. [2] “And it shall be, if the wrongdoer is to be struck, that the judge shall cause him to lie down and be struck in his presence with the number of blows according to his wrong. [3] “Forty strikes he gives him but no more, lest he strike him with many more blows than these, and your brother be degraded before your eyes.

readings.title: Premial Reward for the Laboring Animal
readings.subtitle: Allowing the ox to partake of the harvest it helps generate.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 25:4] “Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.

readings.title: The Levirate Mandate of Generational Continuity
readings.subtitle: The societal duty to establish the name and inheritance of a deceased brother.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 25:5] “When brothers dwell together, and one of them has died, and has no son, the widow of the dead man shall not become a stranger’s outside. Her husband’s brother does go in to her, and shall take her as his wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her. [6] “And it shall be that the first-born son which she bears does rise up for the name of his dead brother, so that his name is not blotted out of Yisra’ěl. [7] “But if the man does not desire to take <dn>את</dn> his brother’s wife, then let his brother’s wife go up to the gate to the elders, and say, ‘My husband’s brother refuses to raise up a name to his brother in Yisra’ěl, he does not agree to perform the duty of my husband’s brother.’ [8] “The elders of his city shall then call him and speak to him, and he shall stand and say, ‘<dn>I</dn> have no desire to take her,’ [9] then his brother’s wife shall come to him in the presence of the elders, and remove his sandal from his foot, and shall spit in his face, and answer and say, ‘Thus it is done to the man who does not build up <dn>את</dn> his brother’s house.’ [10] “And in Yisra’ěl his name shall be called, ‘The house of him who had his sandal removed.’

readings.title: The Prohibition of Unlawful Genital Assault
readings.subtitle: Immediate penal severance for violating the reproductive center of an opponent.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 25:11] “When men fight with one another, a man and his brother, and the wife of one shall draw near to rescue her husband from the hand of the one striking him, and shall put out her hand and take hold of him by the genitals, [12] then you shall cut off <dn>את</dn> her hand – your eye does not pardon.

readings.title: The Absolute Standard of Economic Weights
readings.subtitle: Mandating systemic financial honesty to ensure prolonged days on the soil.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 25:13] “You shall not have in your bag differing weights, a heavy and a light. [14] “You shall not have in your house differing measures, a large and a small. [15] “You shall have a perfect and right weight, a perfect and right measure, so that they prolong your days on the soil which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you. [16] “For all who do these, and all who do unrighteously, are an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: The Total Eradication of Amalek
readings.subtitle: A divine decree to blot out the memory of those who systemically attack the weak.
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 25:17] “Remember <dn>את</dn> what Amalěq did to you on the way as you were coming out of Mitsrayim, [18] how he met you on the way and attacked your back, all the feeble ones in your rear, when you were tired and weary. And he did not fear <dn>Elohim</dn>. [19] “Therefore it shall be, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you rest from your enemies all around, in the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you to possess as an inheritance, that you blot out <dn>את</dn> the remembrance of Amalěq from under the heavens. Do not forget!
